meta.title: North, Central or South Vietnam? How to Plan the Right Trip for You
meta.description:
Planning your first trip to Vietnam? Before you copy an itinerary that squeezes Hanoi, Ha Long Bay, Da Nang, Phu Quoc and Ho Chi Minh City into seven days, watch this.

In this Vietnam travel guide for first-time visitors, I’m breaking down North, Central and South Vietnam so you can decide which region actually belongs in your itinerary. We’ll compare the regions based on the number of days you have, your travel month, interests, budget and how much moving around you are comfortable with.

You’ll find realistic route ideas for a 7-day Vietnam itinerary, along with advice for travellers planning a 10-day, 12-day or two-week Vietnam trip.

In this video, we cover:

• How many regions you can realistically visit
• A North Vietnam itinerary covering Hanoi, Ninh Binh, Ha Long Bay, Lan Ha Bay, Sapa and the Ha Giang Loop
• A Central Vietnam itinerary covering Da Nang, Hoi An, Hue and Phong Nha
• A South Vietnam itinerary covering Ho Chi Minh City, the Mekong Delta, Phu Quoc and Da Lat
• Which part of Vietnam is best for families, couples, honeymooners and food lovers
• The best time to visit Vietnam
• Vietnam travel costs, domestic flights and hidden transfer expenses
• How to choose between North, Central and South Vietnam

This is not an itinerary designed to help you tick off the maximum number of places. It is a practical guide to planning a Vietnam trip that still feels like a holiday.

If you’re still confused, comment with these four things:

Your travel month
The number of full days you have
What you want most from the holiday
Your approximate budget

I’ll help you decide which Vietnam region to prioritise.
